functions.description: Internal helper that enforces pybind11's keep_alive<Nurse, Patient> call policy by creating lifetime ties between a designated "nurse" object and a "patient" object involved in a bound function call. It is invoked either before the actual C++ call (precall) or after it (postcall), depending on whether Nurse and Patient are nonzero or whether one of them refers to the return value (0). Callers pass the current invocation context (function_call) and, when applicable, the function’s return handle.

When both Nurse and Patient are nonzero, this function is intended to be called before the underlying function invocation; in this case ret should be an empty/invalid handle.
When either Nurse or Patient is 0 (refers to the return value), this function is intended to be called after the function invocation; in this case ret must be a valid handle to the return object.
The function_call reference must correspond to the currently executing bound call and remain valid for the duration of this operation.
Indices used (Nurse/Patient when nonzero) must be within the bounds of the actual arguments available in function_call; out-of-range use is invalid.

requirements: The Python GIL must be held when calling (uses CPython C-API and Python-level isinstance).
src must reference a valid (non-null) Python object.
If src is not a dict, it must be a mapping-like object that has a callable items() method to be accepted (unless convert is true and it is derived from collections.abc.Mapping).
This check does not ensure key/value element convertibility to the C++ key/value types.

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::forward_like
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
constexpr forwarded_type<T, U> forward_like(U &&u)
functions.description: Forwards a value u as lvalue or rvalue based on whether T is an lvalue or rvalue reference type. Useful for forwarding container elements while preserving value category relative to another type.
requirements: T and U must be such that forwarded_type<T, U> is a valid type (i.e., remove_reference_t<U> must be well-formed).
u must be convertible to forwarded_type<T, U>.
No runtime preconditions; this is constexpr and exception-free by design.

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::vector_to_array_impl
functions.signature:
template <typename ArrayType, typename V, size_t... I>
ArrayType vector_to_array_impl(V &&v, index_sequence<I...>)
functions.description: Constructs an ArrayType by moving (std::move) elements v[I] for the provided index sequence. Used internally to convert an indexable sequence into a fixed-size array-like type via aggregate initialization.
requirements: V must provide operator[] for all indices I in the index_sequence and those element expressions must be movable (or copyable if move falls back to copy).
ArrayType must be aggregate-initializable from exactly sizeof...(I) elements of the type of v[I].
The sequence v must contain at least max(I)+1 elements; accessing out of range is undefined behavior.
Passing an lvalue v will still attempt to move its elements (std::move(v[I])); those elements must tolerate being moved-from.

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::vector_to_array
functions.signature:

ArrayType vector_to_array(V &&v)
functions.description: Converts an indexable sequence v to ArrayType by moving the first N elements into the resulting array-like type. A thin wrapper that generates index_sequence<0,1,...,N-1> and calls vector_to_array_impl.
requirements: V must provide operator[] and contain at least N elements; accessing fewer than N elements is undefined behavior.
ArrayType must be aggregate-initializable from N elements compatible with the type of v[0].
Elements must be movable (or copyable if move elides to copy).

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::operator<<
functions.description: Streams the string representation of a Python object to a C++ std::ostream by obtaining pybind11::str(obj) and inserting it into os. Uses std::string_view when available, otherwise std::string.
requirements: The Python GIL must be held (converts the Python object to a string).
obj must reference a valid (non-null) Python object; conversion to str must succeed or a pybind11::error_already_set may be thrown.
os must be a valid output stream reference.

functions.name: pybind11::detail::args_any_are_buffer
functions.description: Returns true at compile-time if any type in Args... is pybind11::buffer_protocol. Used to conditionally enable buffer interface bindings for containers. Call in SFINAE contexts or as a constexpr boolean.
requirements: Callable in a constant-evaluated context (constexpr).
Template parameters may be any types; returns true if any are exactly buffer_protocol.

functions.name: pybind11::bind_vector
functions.signature:
template <typename Vector, typename holder_type = default_holder_type<Vector>, typename... Args>
pybind11::class_<Vector, holder_type> pybind11::bind_vector(pybind11::handle scope, const std::string &name, Args&&... args);
functions.description: Creates Python bindings for a C++ vector-like container type (typically std::vector<T>). It defines common Python list-like behavior (construction, iteration, indexing, slicing, append/extend/insert/pop, contains/count/remove, len/bool, repr when << is available) and optionally the buffer protocol. Invoke inside a pybind11 module to expose Vector to Python under the given name.
requirements: Must be called while holding the Python GIL (pybind11 binding creation requires the GIL).

Vector must provide: value_type, size_type, difference_type, iterator, begin(), end(), size(), empty(), data() (only if buffer protocol is requested), operator[] (by value or reference), push_back(), clear(), insert(), erase(), reserve(), shrink_to_fit() (shrink_to_fit() is called in an exception cleanup path; it may throw and is caught).
Vector::value_type must be castable to/from Python (either via an existing pybind11 binding or a type_caster).

If buffer_protocol is passed in Args..., Vector must have data() returning value_type*, and a format_descriptor<value_type> must exist (PYBIND11_NUMPY_DTYPE or a builtin); otherwise compilation will fail.
Equality-based methods (==, !=, count, remove, __contains__) are generated only if Vector or its recursively-checked value types are comparable (operator== is instantiable).
Copy-related methods (copy constructor exposure, modifiers like append/extend/insert/pop/slice-assign) are generated only if Vector::value_type is copy-constructible.
The pretty __repr__ is generated only if operator<<(std::ostream&, const value_type&) is available.
Indexing and slicing operations raise Python index_error on out-of-range access; callers should be prepared for Python exceptions.
The returned class_ must remain in scope (bind within a module variable).

functions.name: pybind11::detail::format_message_key_error_key_object
functions.description: Builds a human-readable string for a KeyError message based on a Python object handle. Attempts str(py_key), falling back to repr(py_key) if needed; truncates very long strings by keeping a prefix and suffix separated by a scissor marker.
requirements: Must be called while holding the Python GIL (performs Python API operations: str, repr, len, slicing).
py_key may be a null handle; in that case a default message 'pybind11::bind_map key' is used.
May raise and catch internal exceptions; function itself returns a pybind11::str and does not propagate exceptions unless underlying API misuse occurs.

functions.name: pybind11::detail::format_message_key_error
functions.description: Constructs a KeyError message string for a C++ key by attempting to cast the key to a Python object and delegating to format_message_key_error_key_object. If casting fails, falls back to a generic message.
requirements: Must be called while holding the Python GIL (casts to Python and may invoke Python API).
KeyType should be castable to Python via pybind11::cast; if not, a generic message is produced without throwing.

functions.name: pybind11::bind_map
functions.signature:
template <typename Map, typename holder_type = default_holder_type<Map>, typename... Args>
pybind11::class_<Map, holder_type> pybind11::bind_map(pybind11::handle scope, const std::string &name, Args&&... args);
functions.description: Creates Python bindings for a C++ associative container with key/value pairs (e.g., std::map<K,V> or std::unordered_map<K,V>). It exposes Python dict-like behavior: len/bool, iteration over keys, views (keys, values, items), __getitem__/__setitem__/__delitem__/__contains__, and repr when stream insertion is available.
requirements: Must be called while holding the Python GIL (pybind11 binding creation requires the GIL).

Map must provide: key_type, mapped_type, begin(), end(), size(), empty(), find(const key_type&), emplace(const key_type&, const mapped_type&), erase(iterator) or erase(key), and iterators compatible with pybind11 make_*_iterator.
Map::mapped_type must be castable to/from Python; Map::key_type must be castable to/from Python for __getitem__/__setitem__/__contains__ to work on typed keys.
__setitem__ is provided only if mapped_type is copy-assignable or at least copy-constructible; in the latter case, assignment is implemented by erase+emplace.
__getitem__ and __delitem__ raise Python KeyError when the key is not present; callers should be prepared for Python exceptions.
The pretty __repr__ is provided only if both operator<<(std::ostream&, const key_type&) and operator<<(std::ostream&, const mapped_type&) are available.
Returned class_ must remain in scope; bind within the module definition.

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::deregister_instance
functions.signature: inline bool deregister_instance(instance *self, void *valptr, const type_info *tinfo);
functions.description: Removes/deregisters a C++ instance association from a pybind11 Python object. Intended to be called when a bound object's lifetime ends so that internal instance lookups no longer find the released C++ value. Return value indicates whether a deregistration actually occurred. Implementation details are not present in this header; behavior is inferred from the name, parameters, and call site in the trampoline_self_life_support destructor.
requirements: Must be called while the Python GIL is held (inferred from usage pattern in the destructor where GIL is ensured before calling).
self must point to a valid pybind11::detail::instance corresponding to the Python object being deregistered (inferred from parameter name and usage).
valptr must be a non-null pointer to the C++ value previously associated with self (inferred; destructor ensures non-null before calling).
tinfo must be a non-null pointer to the correct type_info describing the held C++ type (inferred from typical pybind11 internals).
Caller should check the returned bool to determine if a deregistration actually occurred (inferred from return type).

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::trampoline_self_life_support::activate_life_support
functions.description: Begins "life support" for a trampoline/self object by increasing the Python object's refcount and capturing the provided value_and_holder describing the bound C++ object. Use this when establishing a trampoline so the Python instance stays alive while C++ callbacks may reference it.
requirements: Must be called while the Python GIL is held because it calls Py_INCREF (inferred from direct CPython API usage).
v_h_.inst must be a valid, non-null PyObject* (inferred; Py_INCREF on null is invalid).
v_h_ must describe a live pybind11 instance/value (inferred; storing stale data leads to undefined behavior when later released).
Should not be called repeatedly without a matching deactivate_life_support; repeated activation would leak a reference (inferred from refcount semantics).

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::trampoline_self_life_support::deactivate_life_support
functions.description: Ends "life support" for a trampoline/self object by decrementing the Python object's refcount and resetting the stored value_and_holder to a default-initialized state. Use this to release the extra reference acquired by activate_life_support once the trampoline no longer needs to keep the Python object alive.
requirements: Must be called while the Python GIL is held because it calls Py_DECREF (inferred from direct CPython API usage).
Must only be called after a successful activate_life_support; v_h.inst must be valid and non-null when called (inferred; Py_DECREF on null is invalid).
After calling, the internal value_and_holder becomes default-initialized; do not reuse the previous references (explicit from implementation).

functions.name: pybind11::detail::type_caster<PyObject>::cast
functions.signature:
template <typename T, pybind11::detail::enable_if_t<!pybind11::detail::is_same_ignoring_cvref<T, PyObject *>::value, int> = 0>
static pybind11::handle cast(T &&value, pybind11::return_value_policy policy, pybind11::handle parent)
functions.description: SFINAE-guarded overload meant to prevent accidental attempts to convert arbitrary C++ types to Python via type_caster<PyObject>. If this overload is ever selected/instantiated, it triggers a compile-time static_assert failure. It is not intended for use and has no valid runtime behavior.
requirements: This function must not be used; any instantiation will fail at compile time via static_assert.

No valid combination of template arguments is intended; the only way the static_assert would pass is for T to be PyObject*, in which case this overload is disabled by SFINAE and the other overload applies.

functions.name: pybind11::detail::type_caster<PyObject>::load
functions.description: Loads a Python object from a pybind11 handle into this type_caster by storing it as an internal pybind11::object (borrowed). Always returns true to indicate the value was accepted. Typically used during argument conversion from Python to C++.
requirements: Caller should pass a valid pybind11::handle referring to a live PyObject (inferred from usage of reinterpret_borrow<object>).
Caller should ensure the Python interpreter is initialized and the GIL is held when passing/handling Python objects (inferred from pybind11 usage).
No type checking or error reporting is performed; the function unconditionally returns true.

functions.name: pybind11::detail::type_caster<PyObject>::operator PyObject *
functions.description: Conversion operator that returns the underlying PyObject* stored by this type_caster. Used by pybind11 internals when emitting C++ values back to Python or accessing the raw pointer.
requirements: Must be called only after a successful load() or other initialization that sets an internal object; otherwise value.ptr() may be nullptr (inferred from implementation).
Caller should hold the Python GIL when accessing raw PyObject* pointers (inferred from pybind11/Python API usage).

functions.name: pybind11::detail::PyWarning_Check
functions.description: Checks whether a given Python object is a subclass of PyExc_Warning. Internally calls PyObject_IsSubclass(obj, PyExc_Warning) and returns true if obj is a warning category, false if not. If the subclass check triggers a Python error, it raises a SystemError and throws pybind11::error_already_set. Use this to validate warning categories passed from C++ into pybind11/Python APIs.
requirements: obj must be a non-null PyObject*.
obj should refer to a Python class/type (or an object acceptable to PyObject_IsSubclass); otherwise the subclass check may raise and this function will throw error_already_set.
The Python interpreter must be initialized and the GIL must be held when calling (inferred from use of the Python C API via pybind11).
Callers should be prepared to catch pybind11::error_already_set if PyObject_IsSubclass fails (e.g., due to an invalid obj).

functions.name: pybind11::warnings::new_warning_type
functions.signature: pybind11::object pybind11::warnings::new_warning_type(pybind11::handle scope, const char *name, pybind11::handle base = PyExc_RuntimeWarning)
functions.description: Creates a new custom Python Warning class (type) and installs it as an attribute on the given scope (e.g., a module). The full qualified name is built as scope.__name__ + "." + name. The base must be a subclass of PyExc_Warning. On creation failure it throws pybind11::error_already_set; on invalid inputs it calls pybind11_fail (terminating via exception). Returns the new warning type object and assigns it to scope[name].
requirements: scope must be a valid pybind11::handle referring to an object with a __name__ attribute and supporting attribute assignment (commonly a module).
name must be a non-null C string; an attribute with the same name must not already exist in scope (the function checks hasattr and fails if it does).
base must be a warning category: a subclass of PyExc_Warning; otherwise the function fails with pybind11_fail.
The Python interpreter must be initialized and the GIL must be held when calling (inferred from Python C API usage).
Callers must handle exceptions: pybind11_fail will throw; if PyErr_NewException fails, the function raises a SystemError and throws pybind11::error_already_set.

functions.name: pybind11::warnings::warn
functions.signature: void pybind11::warnings::warn(const char *message, pybind11::handle category = PyExc_RuntimeWarning, int stack_level = 2)
functions.description: Emits a Python warning, similar to Python's warnings.warn(). The message is the warning text; category is the warning class (must be a subclass of PyExc_Warning); stack_level controls where the warning appears to originate. If PyErr_WarnEx returns -1 (e.g., warning converted to error), it throws pybind11::error_already_set.
requirements: message must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
category must be a warning category: a subclass of PyExc_Warning; otherwise the function fails with pybind11_fail.
stack_level is an integer; larger values report the warning as coming from higher up the call stack (behavior analogous to Python warnings.warn).
The Python interpreter must be initialized and the GIL must be held when calling (inferred from Python C API usage).
Callers should be prepared to catch pybind11::error_already_set if the warning emission results in a Python error (e.g., if warnings are treated as errors).

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::path_caster<T>::cast
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::handle PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::path_caster<T>::cast(const T &path, PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::return_value_policy, PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::handle parent)
functions.description: Converts a C++ filesystem path (T) into a Python pathlib.Path object. It encodes the path using Python’s filesystem encoding (via PyUnicode_* APIs) from the path’s native() representation, constructs pathlib.Path from it, and returns a new Python handle. Typical usage is within pybind11’s type conversion when returning a std::filesystem::path (or experimental equivalent) back to Python. The return_value_policy and parent parameters are part of the caster interface and are not used by this implementation.
requirements: Must be called with the Python GIL held (uses Python C API functions like PyUnicode_* and module import).

Template parameter T must be a filesystem path-like type whose native() returns std::basic_string<char> or std::basic_string<wchar_t> (e.g., std::filesystem::path or std::experimental::filesystem::path).
On success returns a new reference to a Python object (pathlib.Path); the caller (pybind11 internals) take ownership of the returned handle.
If Python object creation fails, returns a null handle.

functions.name: PYBIND11_NAMESPACE::detail::path_caster<T>::load
functions.description: Parses a Python path-like object (os.PathLike, str, or bytes) into a C++ filesystem path of type T for use by pybind11 argument conversion. It first normalizes the input using PyOS_FSPath, then decodes to either bytes (char) or wide string (wchar_t) depending on T::value_type, and assigns the resulting native path into the caster’s value member. Returns true on success, false on failure. Errors raised during intermediate steps are cleared and cause a false return.
requirements: Must be called with the Python GIL held (uses Python C API functions: PyOS_FSPath, PyUnicode_FSConverter, PyUnicode_FSDecoder, etc.).
Input parameter must be a valid Python object representing an os.PathLike, str, or bytes; otherwise PyOS_FSPath may fail and the function returns false.
Template parameter T must have value_type equal to char or wchar_t (the implementation only handles these two cases).
On success, the caster’s internal value (inherited from PYBIND11_TYPE_CASTER) is set to the decoded path; callers should read that value after a true return.
The function manages and decrements temporary Python references it creates; callers must not use them after the call.
On failure, the function clears any Python error and returns false; callers should not expect a Python exception to be set.

functions.name: pybind11_conduit_v1::get_raw_pointer_ephemeral
functions.description: Retrieves a raw C++ pointer for a Python object that exposes the _pybind11_conduit_v1_ conduit. Internally, it wraps cpp_type_info in a capsule, calls py_obj->_pybind11_conduit_v1_(PYBIND11_PLATFORM_ABI_ID, cpp_type_info_capsule, "raw_pointer_ephemeral"), then extracts the pointer from the returned capsule using cpp_type_info->name(). Returns nullptr on any failure (e.g., method missing, ABI/type mismatch, Python error). The returned pointer is ephemeral: its lifetime is tied to py_obj’s lifetime.
requirements: py_obj must be a valid, non-null PyObject* instance.
py_obj must implement a method named _pybind11_conduit_v1_(self, pybind11_platform_abi_id: bytes, cpp_type_info_capsule: capsule, pointer_kind: bytes) -> capsule.
The provided cpp_type_info must point to the std::type_info of the desired C++ type (typically &typeid(T)); it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
The conduit implementation must return a capsule whose name matches cpp_type_info->name() and whose pointer is the underlying C++ object pointer.
The Python interpreter must be initialized and the calling thread must hold the GIL when invoking this function (required by Python/C API usage).
The returned pointer must not be dereferenced after py_obj is destroyed; the pointer is only valid for the lifetime of py_obj (ephemeral).
Callers must check the return value for nullptr before use. On failure, a Python exception may be set (PyErr_Occurred).

functions.name: pybind11_conduit_v1::get_type_pointer_ephemeral
functions.description: Type-safe wrapper around get_raw_pointer_ephemeral that requests a pointer to T. It queries the conduit using &typeid(T) and returns a T* on success or nullptr on failure. The pointer is ephemeral and valid only while py_obj remains alive.
requirements: py_obj must be a valid, non-null PyObject* instance.
py_obj must implement the _pybind11_conduit_v1_ method compatible with the conduit contract (accepts platform ABI id, type_info capsule, and pointer kind "raw_pointer_ephemeral").
T must correspond to the actual C++ type (or a compatible type) wrapped by py_obj as recognized by the conduit; otherwise nullptr will be returned.
The Python interpreter must be initialized and the calling thread must hold the GIL when invoking this function.
The returned T* is only valid for the lifetime of py_obj (ephemeral) and must not be used after py_obj is destroyed.
Callers must check for nullptr before dereferencing. On failure, a Python exception may be set by the underlying calls.

# and strings with embedded nulls avoided (since most stubs pass c_str()).
#
# Strategy:
# - Randomly choose from themed constructors to cover:
#   * Printable ASCII, including punctuation
#   * Whitespace squashing cases (newlines, tabs, spaces)
#   * Python format strings with placeholders (for str.format tests)
#   * Valid Python identifiers for submodule/class names
#   * File-system-like paths (both POSIX and Windows style)
#   * Repetition/long strings for truncation logic
#   * Bytes-like content shown as escaped to remain valid UTF-8
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic under the provided seed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=200) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces occasionally to test trimming behavior distinctly
    if length > 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = s.strip(' ')
    return s


def _rand_whitespace_heavy(rng: random.Random, max_len=300) -> str:
    parts = []
    # Mix tabs, spaces, newlines; include quoted sections to avoid squashing
    tokens = [
        '   ', '\t', '\n', ' \t\n ', "'keep this as-is'", 'word', 'another', '123'
    ]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(tokens))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s


def _rand_format_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid Python format strings with positional fields
    patterns = [
        '{}', '{0}', '{1}{}', '{}-{}-{}', '{:>10}', '{!s}:{!r}', '{}:{}', '{:0.2f}', '{:x}', '{:d}',
    ]
    # Build a mixed pattern
    s = rng.choice(patterns)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s += '-' + rng.choice(patterns)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = s * rng.randint(2, 4)
    return s[:512]


def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, max_len=32) -> str:
    first = string.ascii_letters + '_'
    rest = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_'
    n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(first) + ''.join(rng.choice(rest) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix POSIX and Windows style
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # POSIX
        parts = [
            '',  # leading slash
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8),
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8),
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8) + ('.txt' if rng.random() < 0.5 else ''),
        ]
        path = '/'.join(parts)
    else:
        # Windows
        drive = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) + ':\\'
        comps = [
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8),
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8),
            _rand_identifier(rng, 8) + ('.bin' if rng.random() < 0.5 else ''),
        ]
        path = drive + '\\'.join(comps)
    return path


def _rand_repeated(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 40)
    reps = rng.randint(10, 80)
    s = (base + '\n') * reps
    return s[:2000]


def _rand_bytes_escaped(rng: random.Random, min_len=10, max_len=200) -> str:
    # Generate random bytes and escape non-printables to keep a valid UTF-8 string
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    b = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
    out_chars: List[str] = []
    for ch in b:
        if 32 <= ch < 127 and ch != 92:  # printable non-backslash
            out_chars.append(chr(ch))
        elif ch == 92:  # backslash
            out_chars.append('\\\\')
        elif ch == 9:
            out_chars.append('\\t')
        elif ch == 10:
            out_chars.append('\\n')
        elif ch == 13:
            out_chars.append('\\r')
        else:
            out_chars.append(f"\\x{ch:02x}")
    s = ''.join(out_chars)
    return s[:512]


def _merge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose multiple pieces to increase coverage in a single buffer
    parts = []
    choices = [
        _rand_ascii(rng),
        _rand_whitespace_heavy(rng),
        _rand_format_string(rng),
        _rand_identifier(rng),
        _rand_path(rng),
        _rand_repeated(rng),
        _rand_bytes_escaped(rng),
    ]
    rng.shuffle(choices)
    for s in choices[:rng.randint(2, 5)]:
        parts.append(s)
    sep = '\n' if rng.random() < 0.7 else ' '
    combined = sep.join(parts)
    # Ensure no embedded NULs since many stubs pass c_str()
    combined = combined.replace('\x00', '_')
    # Limit total size
    return combined[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.12:
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 512)
    elif mode < 0.24:
        s = _rand_whitespace_heavy(rng)
    elif mode < 0.36:
        s = _rand_format_string(rng)
    elif mode < 0.48:
        s = _rand_identifier(rng)
    elif mode < 0.60:
        s = _rand_path(rng)
    elif mode < 0.72:
        s = _rand_repeated(rng)
    elif mode < 0.84:
        s = _rand_bytes_escaped(rng)
    else:
        s = _merge_cases(rng)

    # Final sanitation: cap size and avoid embedded NULs
    if len(s) > MAX_TOTAL:
        s = s[:MAX_TOTAL]
    s = s.replace('\x00', '_')
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: Python identifier string
# Many stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR to form identifiers (module/submodule names, exception names, class names).
# We generate a small corpus of valid identifiers with variations to exercise different code paths:
# - lengths: short, medium, max-ish (<= 32/64 as seen in sanitizers)
# - character sets: letters, digits (not first), underscores, mixed case
# - edge cases: starting underscore, near-limit lengths, with digits later
# The generator returns a bytes buffer that the fuzzer runtime will split to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# multiple times. We concatenate multiple identifiers separated by newlines so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# can consume one slice deterministically.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _ident_from_charset(rng: random.Random, length: int, allow_lead_digit: bool = False) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_letters
    digits = string.digits
    tail_chars = letters + digits + "_"
    if allow_lead_digit:
        first_pool = letters + "_" + digits
    else:
        first_pool = letters + "_"
    first = rng.choice(first_pool)
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(tail_chars) for _ in range(max(0, length - 1)))
    return first + rest

def _make_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []

    # Deterministic fixed seeds
    corpus.extend([
        "m",              # minimal valid
        "E",              # single letter for exception names
        "_",              # leading underscore
        "mod",            # common module prefix
        "Class_1",        # mixed with digit later
        "Exc_Fuzz",       # exception-like
        "VectorBind",     # for bind_vector
        "MapBind",        # for bind_map
        "_FZWarn_Base",   # warnings name prefix used in stub
    ])

    # Length variations around 8, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64 (stubs cap 31/32/64 sometimes)
    for L in [1, 2, 8, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64]:
        corpus.append(_ident_from_charset(rng, L, allow_lead_digit=False))

    # Mixed-case and underscore heavy identifiers
    for _ in range(10):
        L = rng.randint(3, 24)
        s = _ident_from_charset(rng, L)
        # randomly sprinkle more underscores
        if L > 4:
            idx = rng.randrange(1, L)
            s = s[:idx] + "_" + s[idx:]
        corpus.append(s)

    # Identifiers starting with underscore (valid and common for private names)
    for _ in range(5):
        L = rng.randint(2, 20)
        corpus.append("_" + _ident_from_charset(rng, L - 1, allow_lead_digit=True))

    # Ensure some begin with letters near ends of ranges
    corpus.extend(["a" + "9" * 5 + "_x", "Z__0x", "m" + "_" * 10 + "n"])

    # Trim to keep total under limit once joined
    return corpus

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = _make_corpus(rng)

    # Shuffle to diversify sequences across seeds
    rng.shuffle(corpus)

    # Many stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice or more; include plenty
    # Join with newlines so each call reads sequential slices.
    data = "\n".join(corpus)

    # Safety: cap total size
    b = data.encode("utf-8")
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure we don't cut in middle of utf-8 (ascii only here, so safe)
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: alphanumeric string used as a module name suffix; non-alphanumerics are filtered out.
# Target fuzzer stub: pybind11::error_already_set::what
# The stub initializes a scoped_interpreter and triggers a Python error by calling a non-callable.
# There are no FUZZ_PARAM_STR or FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME uses in this stub, so the input buffer is unused.
# Nevertheless, we provide a reasonable alphanumeric string payload that could serve as a module name
# suffix in other stubs or harness glue. Keep it <= 4096 bytes.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure it starts with a letter or underscore to be a valid Python identifier piece
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return first + rest

def _interesting_suffixes() -> List[str]:
    # A small set of interesting names that are valid and might explore cache/lookup paths
    return [
        "pybind11_test",
        "module",
        "__main__",
        "m",
        "A1_",
        "x" * 16,
        "Test123_ABC",
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose a mix of deterministic interesting strings and a random one, joined with a separator
    parts = []
    base_choices = _interesting_suffixes()
    rng.shuffle(base_choices)
    # Take a random number of base choices
    k = rng.randint(1, min(4, len(base_choices)))
    parts.extend(base_choices[:k])

    # Add one or two random alphanumeric tokens
    parts.append(_rand_alnum(rng, 3, 24))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_rand_alnum(rng, 1, 12))

    # Join with a safe delimiter that is also alphanumeric-friendly (underscore)
    payload = "_".join(parts)

    # Ensure length limit
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]

    return payload.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: argv string
# Requirements: Should be decodable by Py_DecodeLocale. That generally means valid
# UTF-8 in most environments or ASCII-safe bytes. We'll generate Unicode strings
# with a bias toward typical argv patterns: program paths, flags, options with
# values, environment-like tokens, and varied lengths; but keep within 256 bytes
# since the stub truncates at 256. We will emit a newline-separated corpus of
# candidate argv strings, so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can pick from it.
#
# The fuzzer stub constructs up to 3 argv entries (s0..s2) from FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# To maximize interesting behavior, we provide multiple well-formed tokens per
# buffer, separated by NULs, newlines, and ASCII unit separators, allowing the
# fuzzer infra to split or slice as it sees fit. We avoid malformed encodings.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:@+,%"

COMMON_FLAGS = [
    "-h", "--help", "-V", "--version", "-v", "-vv", "-Wignore", "-Werror",
    "-B", "-E", "-Iinclude", "-mjson.tool", "-mhttp.server", "-O", "-OO",
]

COMMON_OPTS = [
    "--option=value", "--threads=4", "--log-level=debug", "--log-level=INFO",
    "--path=/tmp", "--path=./relative", "--config=config.cfg",
]

# Some plausible program names/paths
PROGRAMS = [
    "python", "python3", "pypy3", "C:/Python39/python.exe", "/usr/bin/python3",
    "./prog", "my_tool", "äöü-script", "项目/程序", "スペース/プログラム",
]

# Some filenames that are portable UTF-8
FILENAMES = [
    "script.py", "-", "README.md", "data.txt", "input.json", "テスト.py",
    "παράδειγμα.py", "документ.txt", "配置.yaml", "config-测试.ini",
]

UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "café", "naïve", "smörgåsbord", "mañana", "façade", "niño", "über",
    "Здравствуйте", "こんにちは", "مرحبا", "שלום", "हैलो", "γειά", "안녕하세요",
]

SEPARATORS = ["\n", "\0", "\x1f", " "]


def _rand_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights=None) -> str:
    if not items:
        return ""
    if weights is None:
        return rng.choice(items)
    # Simple weighted choice
    total = sum(weights)
    t = rng.uniform(0, total)
    c = 0.0
    for w, it in zip(weights, items):
        c += w
        if t <= c:
            return it
    return items[-1]


def _make_safe_token(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII-safe and some Unicode words to exercise Py_DecodeLocale
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
        return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))
    elif choice < 0.8:
        return _rand_weighted_choice(rng, UNICODE_WORDS)
    else:
        # Compose a path-like token
        base = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, PROGRAMS)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # append a subpath or filename
            suf = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, FILENAMES)
            if not base.endswith("/") and not base.endswith("\\"):
                sep = "/" if "/" in base or rng.random() < 0.8 else "\\"
                base = base + sep
            base = base + suf
        return base


def _build_argv_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build 1..3 argv entries, first simulating program name
    argc = rng.randint(1, 3)
    argv: List[str] = []
    # Program name
    prog = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, PROGRAMS)
    argv.append(prog)

    for _ in range(argc - 1):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.35:
            argv.append(_rand_weighted_choice(rng, COMMON_FLAGS))
        elif t < 0.65:
            argv.append(_rand_weighted_choice(rng, COMMON_OPTS))
        else:
            # Free-form token or filename
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                argv.append(_make_safe_token(rng, 40))
            else:
                argv.append(_rand_weighted_choice(rng, FILENAMES))
    # Ensure each entry <= 256 when encoded
    trimmed = []
    for a in argv:
        b = a.encode('utf-8', 'strict')
        if len(b) > 256:
            # Trim at char boundary to <=256
            s = a
            while len(s.encode('utf-8')) > 256 and len(s) > 0:
                s = s[:-1]
            trimmed.append(s)
        else:
            trimmed.append(a)
    return trimmed


def _serialize_argvs(rng: random.Random, argv_sets: List[List[str]]) -> bytes:
    # Combine multiple argv sets into one buffer using varied separators so that
    # multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can pull different slices. We keep the total
    # size <= 4096.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for args in argv_sets:
        sep = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, SEPARATORS, weights=[3, 1, 1, 2])
        # Join args for one logical group with spaces, then separate groups by sep
        group = " ".join(args)
        parts.append(group.encode('utf-8'))
        parts.append(sep.encode('utf-8'))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
        # avoid cutting a UTF-8 sequence: backtrack to valid boundary
        # find last valid prefix
        i = len(data)
        while i > 0:
            try:
                data[:i].decode('utf-8')
                data = data[:i]
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                i -= 1
        if i == 0:
            data = b""
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create several argv sets to populate the buffer; 2..6 groups
    groups = rng.randint(2, 6)
    argv_sets = [_build_argv_set(rng) for _ in range(groups)]

    # Occasionally include empty tokens or lone dashes which are valid argv entries
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        argv_sets.append([_rand_weighted_choice(rng, ["-", "", "--"])])

    buf = _serialize_argvs(rng, argv_sets)
    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not buf:
        buf = b"python -h\n"
    return buf

from typing import List

# Generates valid Python source bytes for eval_file. Keep syntax valid.

_PY_SNIPPETS: List[str] = [
    "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n",
    "import sys, os, math, random, datetime, pathlib, warnings\n",
    "from collections import deque\n",
    "nums = [i for i in range(10)]\n",
    "squared = [n*n for n in nums]\n",
    "d = {str(k): v for k, v in enumerate(squared)}\n",
    "s = set(d.keys())\n",
    "cwd = pathlib.Path(os.getcwd())\n",
    "this_file = pathlib.Path(__file__) if '__file__' in globals() else cwd / 'script.py'\n",
    "_unused_path = (cwd / 'subdir')\n",
    "def gen():\n\tfor i in range(3):\n\t\tyield i\n",
    "g_sum = sum(gen())\n",
    "class C:\n\tdef __init__(self, x): self.x = x\n\tdef __repr__(self): return f'C(x={self.x!r})'\n\tdef __add__(self, other):\n\t\ttry: return C(self.x + other.x)\n\t\texcept Exception: return C(self.x)\n\tdef __iter__(self):\n\t\tyield from (self.x, self.x+1)\n",
    "c = C(5)\n",
    "dq = deque(maxlen=5)\n",
    "for _x in range(7): dq.append(_x)\n",
    "u = 'αβγ'\n",
    # Safe bytes literal using escapes
    "b = b'\x00\x01test'\n",
    "try:\n\tif random.random() < 2:\n\t\twarnings.warn('notice', RuntimeWarning)\n\t_ = 1/1\nexcept Exception as e:\n\t_ignored = str(e)\n",
    "now = datetime.datetime.now()\n",
    "_desc = f'len(nums)={len(nums)}, g_sum={g_sum}, cwd={cwd.name}'\n",
    "_contains = ('3' in d) and ('42' not in d)\n",
    "_slice = squared[2:5] if len(squared) >= 5 else squared\n",
    "val = (lambda x: x+1)(3)\n",
]

_RANDOM_SELECTS: List[str] = [
    "for _i in range(2):\n\tpass\n",
    "with open(__file__, 'rb') if '__file__' in globals() else open(os.devnull, 'rb') as _f:\n\t_ = _f.read(0)\n",
    "path_join = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'a', 'b')\n",
    "p = pathlib.Path(os.getcwd()) / 'x' / 'y'\n",
    "def _f(a:int, b:int=2, *args, **kwargs):\n\treturn a + b + len(args) + len(kwargs)\n",
    "_r = list(map(lambda x: x+1, range(5)))\n",
    "_c = {k:v for k,v in d.items()}\n",
]

def _build_script(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.extend(_PY_SNIPPETS)
    opt = _RANDOM_SELECTS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(opt)
    take = rng.randint(1, min(4, len(opt)))
    parts.extend(opt[:take])
    parts.append("None\n")
    script = "".join(parts)
    enc = script.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
    if len(enc) > 4000:
        # Trim to stay under the limit without cutting mid-line too much
        script = script[:3500]
    return script


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    script = _build_script(rng)
    return script.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
